lit.\u0027¿Cuál se conserva en toda reacción: "Which is conserved in every nuclear reaction?"
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eA = Z + N\u003c/b\u00: "A = Z + N; A and the charge are conserved."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl núcleo contiene \u:
"

The nucleus contains protons (Z) and neutrons (N); A = Z + N is the mass number. The isotopes of an element have the same Z and different N. Carbon-14 has Z = 6, N = 8, A = 14. Nucleons are held together by the strong nuclear force, which exceeds the electrostatic repulsion between protons only at distances of ~1 fm.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn \u003cb\u003eβ⁻\u0:
"

In β⁻ a neutron becomes a proton: Z rises by 1 and A stays (¹⁴C → ¹⁴N + e⁻ + ν̄). In β⁺ a proton becomes a neutron (¹⁸F → ¹⁸O + e⁺ + ν, used in PET scans). In electron capture the nucleus absorbs an electron from its shell (⁴⁰K → ⁴⁰Ar). A and the total charge are always conserved.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la \u003cb\u003eem:
"

In α emission the nucleus expels a particle of 2 protons and 2 neutrons: ᴬ_Z X → ᴬ⁻⁴_(Z−2) Y + ⁴₂He. Example: ²³⁸U → ²³⁴Th + α. It is typical of heavy nuclei. The α particle is highly ionizing but barely penetrating: a sheet of paper stops it.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa desintegración es:
"

Decay is a random first-order process: each nucleus has the same probability λ per unit time. After each half-life (t½) half remains: N = N₀·(½)^(t/t½), with λ = ln 2 / t½. The activity A = λN is measured in becquerel (1 Bq = 1 decay/s). Each dot in the panel is an atom; the blue ones have already decayed.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos núcleos estables:
"

Stable nuclei form the band of stability in the N–Z plane: N ≈ Z up to Z ≈ 20 and then N/Z grows (≈ 1.5 in lead) because more neutrons are needed to offset the repulsion between protons. With too many neutrons the nucleus emits β⁻; with too many protons, β⁺ or electron capture; heavy nuclei (Z > 83) emit α. All with Z > 83 are radioactive.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos seres vivos incor:
"

Living things take up ¹⁴C (formed by cosmic rays in the atmosphere) and maintain a constant fraction. On dying, the ¹⁴C decays with t½ = 5730 years: age = (t½/ln 2)·ln(N₀/N). It works up to ≈ 50,000 years (≈ 9 half-lives); for older samples isotopes with longer half-lives are used (U-Pb, K-Ar).

"
